title: Design a content-preserving Aria to VCF management migration
prompt:
Architecture delivery for our two-site management estate. Produce the target architecture and ordered migration plan as `architecture.json`, and implement the Go package at the module root that loads and validates that artifact against the supplied estate and compatibility data. This is an architecture deliverable, not a prose report.

Before implementing it, use the harness's real network research tools to consult currently reachable, official Broadcom-published sources. Research the supported paths from the exact vRealize/Aria versions in `testdata/estate_inventory.json` to VCF Operations, VCF Automation, and VCF Operations for Logs; content and configuration compatibility; and the applicable end-of-general-support boundaries. Record every source you actually consulted in `architecture.json` under `research`, with its title, URL, consultation date, and the decisions it informed. Do not substitute the pinned snapshot for this live research. The research must be genuine; do not create a mock search or fetch service. No particular query or URL is prescribed.

For deterministic design values, `testdata/compatibility_snapshot.json` is the authority if a live page has changed. `testdata/architecture_schema.json` fixes the artifact schema. Model that schema in package `vcfarch` and expose `LoadArchitecture(io.Reader)`, `LoadInventory(io.Reader)`, `LoadCompatibilitySnapshot(io.Reader)`, and `Validate(Architecture, EstateInventory, CompatibilitySnapshot)`. Loaders must reject unknown fields and trailing JSON. Validation must derive the design from the fixture and snapshot rather than special-casing the finished artifact.

The artifact must place and size every target component in the stretched management domain across both data sites. Place the vSAN witness at the independent tertiary site, never at either data site and never as a target-component location. Honor the fixture's PFTT, SFTT, RAID policy, and current host inventory; the host design must actually support the stated failures-to-tolerate. Use the snapshot's demand bands to select each target size and node count, distribute nodes across the two sites, and include anti-affinity.

Create one ordered migration step for every source product in the inventory. Each step must name the inventory id, full source product and version, support boundary, target component and version, supported version path and migration method, dependencies, placement reference, every required gate, and a complete disposition for every inventoried content/configuration item. State what carries forward and by which compatible method, and what is abandoned with a non-empty reason. Content must appear exactly once, with no omissions or inventions.

`architecture_test.go` and everything under `testdata/` are protected and must not be modified. Acceptance is `go test -race -timeout 30s ./...`.
